text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- SOY EXPORTS WILL TOTAL $5.2 BILLION IN '97
Brazil's soy crop will amount to some 27 million tonnes this year, bringing in $5.2 billion in export revenue.
-- GREENSPAN SIGNALS NEW INTEREST RATE HIKE
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan hinted at the likelihood of an upcoming interest rate hike due to inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy.
-- EMBRAER TO DEVELOP TWO NEW REGIONAL JETS
Brazilian aerospace firm Embraer will invest $550 million to develop two new regional jet airlines.
O GLOBO
-- NEW DOCUMENT LINKS SAO PAULO MAYOR TO BOND SCAM

A document discovered by investigators looking into a multi-million dollar bond scam shows that Sao Paulo Mayor Celso Pitta authorized Banco do Brasil to sell $70 million in municipal bonds to Banco Vetor, a brokerage house tied to the scandal. The document contradicts previous statements by Pitta, who has denied doing any business with Vetor.
-- MURDERS OF MINORS ON THE RISE IN RIO

The number of minors who were murdered grew 10 percent in 1996 over 1995 in the state of Rio de Janeiro. Authorities said 659 children were murdered in 1996 in the state, compared to 596 the year before.
-- POLL SAYS 85 PCT OF BRAZILIANS SUPPORT LAND INVASIONS
A new poll by Ibope has found that 85 percent of Brazilians are in favor of landless rural workers taking over and farming unused arable land.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- PENSION REFORM LEADER SEES RETIREMENT AGE RISING
Social Security Minister Reinhold Stephanes said that in the future it will be necessary to raise the minimum retirement age for men to 65 years.
-- SENATE COMMISSION APPROVES BOND ISSUES FOR SANTA CATARINA

A Senate commission has approved a plan by the state of Santa Catarina to issue 33 million reais in bonds. Senator Vilson Kleinubing, who is leading a separate investigation into a multi-million dollar municipal and state bond scandal, chaired the commission to authorize Santa Catarina's bond deal.
* Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
((--John Miller, Sao Paulo newsroom, 5511 248-5414))
